cases.name: blockquote
cases.note: The reference slices `state.src` without removing blockquote markers, so the `>` prefix leaks into the diagram source; the current package strips it through `getLines`. The blockquote structure is identical.
cases.ourHtml:

block markup="@startuml" params="" title="" map=0..2 content="Bob -> Alice : hello"
cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1

cases.name: nested-blockquote
cases.note: Same cause as `blockquote`: the reference keeps both `> >` prefixes in the diagram source, the current package strips both quote levels. The nested blockquote structure is identical.

cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1

cases.name: indented-marker
cases.note: Both sides accept the two-space indented marker, but `dedent` removes the indentation of the content line in the current package while the reference keeps the line as written.
cases.ourHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params="" title="" map=0..2 content="Bob -> Alice : hello"
cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params="" title="" map=0..2 content="  Bob -> Alice : hello"

cases.name: indented-content
cases.note: The current package removes the common indentation of the diagram body, the reference keeps every line as written. `dedent` preserves the relative indentation, so the drawing itself is unchanged.
cases.ourHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params="" title="" map=0..4 content="Alice -> Bob\n  note right\nBob -> Carol"
cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params="" title="" map=0..4 content="  Alice -> Bob\n    note right\n  Bob -> Carol"

cases.name: title
cases.note: The current base keeps the raw marker suffix (including the separating space) as `info`; the reference removes that space and inline-parses the suffix for its alt text, which is the title compared here.
cases.ourHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params=" My title" title=" My title" map=0..2 content="Bob -> Alice : hello"
cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params=" My title" title="My title" map=0..2 content="Bob -> Alice : hello"

cases.name: title-inline-markup
cases.note: Besides the separating space, the reference inline-parses the title, so `**Flow**` disappears from its alt text; the current base keeps the raw markers in `info`.
cases.ourHtml:

cases.referenceHtml:

cases.name: title-only-space
cases.note: The marker is followed by a single space, so the suffix is `" "`: the current base keeps it, while the reference unconditionally drops the first suffix character and ends up with an empty alt text.
cases.ourHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params=" " title=" " map=0..2 content="A -> B"
cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1

cases.name: odd-marker-suffix
cases.note: `@startumlExtra` still matches the opening marker as a prefix on both sides and both report the suffix `Extra` in `info`, but the reference unconditionally drops the first suffix character for its alt text (`xtra`), while the current base keeps the raw suffix as the title.
cases.ourHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params="Extra" title="Extra" map=0..2 content="A -> B"
cases.referenceHtml:
blocks=1
block markup="@startuml" params="Extra" title="xtra" map=0..2 content="A -> B"

cases.name: closing-marker-indented
cases.note: Both sides reject a closing marker indented deeper than the opening one, keep the line as diagram content and auto-close the block at the end of the document.

cases.name: closing-marker-trailing-text
cases.note: Both sides require the closing marker line to contain only spaces after the marker, so the line stays in the diagram source and the block is auto-closed at the end of the document.

notes: `@mdit/plugin-uml` is the generalized base implementation of `markdown-it-plantuml`: it contains the same `@`-marker block rule, line scanning and auto-close rules, with the marker names, the token name and the renderer turned into options. This spec compares only that base block parser; the PlantUML image and encoder layer is out of scope and is disabled on both sides. The marker options are mapped 1:1 — the current side is configured with `{ name: "uml", open: "startuml", close: "enduml", renderer }` and the reference with `{ openMarker: "@startuml", closeMarker: "@enduml", generateSource, render }` — and each plugin registers its rule before `fence` with the same `alt` list, so the two parsers see the same block boundaries.

Rendering is replaced by a deterministic dump on both sides: `blocks=N` followed by the document HTML of the shared markdown-it renderer, with every plugin block token serialized as `block markup=… params=… title=… map=… content=…` (strings JSON-quoted). The output is compared byte for byte (`normalize` is the identity function), because the only real differences are inside that record and the surrounding HTML comes from the same markdown-it core. No encoder, server URL or network access is involved on either side: the current `renderer` option and the reference `render` option return the record, and the reference `generateSource` returns the diagram source unchanged instead of the deflate + base64 server URL.

The reference never stores the diagram source on its token: the block rule passes it to `generateSource` and keeps the result in the `src` attribute, while `token.content` stays empty. The current base stores it in `token.content`. The identity `generateSource` is therefore both the replacement for the encoder and the way the reference's extracted source is read back for the record; the `src`/`alt` attributes and the `` tag are not compared (the current base pushes a placeholder `` token without attributes, and the image markup is the layer this spec excludes).

The reference hard-codes the token type `uml_diagram`, which is also its renderer key. In the current package both are the `name` option (`uml` here, which is also the name `@mdit/plugin-plantuml` passes). The record prints a canonical `block` marker instead of the literal token type so that this naming difference does not mask the field-by-field comparison; the serializer of each side is installed as the renderer rule for its own token type, so a token of an unexpected type would not be rendered at all.

Titles are handled differently by the two implementations. The reference derives an `alt` inside the block rule: it drops the first character of the marker suffix (`params.slice(1)`, assuming a separating space) and inline-parses the rest into `token.children`, falling back to the fixed `uml diagram` when the suffix is empty. The current base derives nothing: it exposes the raw suffix as `token.info` and leaves titles to the renderer (`@mdit/plugin-plantuml` uses that raw suffix as the image alt text). The compared `title` field is therefore the raw `info` on the current side and the inline-rendered alt text on the reference side; the fixed `uml diagram` fallback is not compared because it is an arbitrary label of the disabled image layer (the `plugin-plantuml` comparison covers it). `title`, `title-inline-markup`, `title-only-space` and `odd-marker-suffix` document the remaining differences.

The body is extracted differently: the current package calls `state.getLines(startLine + 1, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` and `dedent`, while the reference slices the raw document with `state.src.split('\n').slice(startLine + 1, nextLine).join('\n')`. Both agree on the line range, the auto-close rules, the block count, the `markup` and the token `map` in every case; they disagree on the text. The reference keeps the indentation of list items and of indented blocks and even the `>` prefixes of blockquotes, while the current package strips the container prefixes and the common indentation. `list-item`, `list-item-unclosed`, `blockquote`, `nested-blockquote`, `indented-marker` and `indented-content` document this; the block structure around the diagrams is identical in all of them.

Both sides reject a closing marker that is indented deeper than the opening one or followed by non-space text, keep that line as diagram content and auto-close the block at the end of the parent; `closing-marker-indented` and `closing-marker-trailing-text` pin this down. Markers inside fences and indented code blocks are not parsed by either side (both rules sit between `code` and `fence`), and an escaped (`\@startuml`) or mid-line marker stays paragraph text on both sides.

Benchmarks use the same deterministic dump, so they measure block parsing and the shared markdown-it rendering only; the deflate + base64 encoder and the network are excluded on both sides. The `heavy` corpora contain four diagrams per section rather than one, so their ratios also include the reference's per-block whole-document split described below.

Scaling: the reference extracts every block with `state.src.split('\n')`, so each block costs O(document) and many blocks cost O(blocks × document) — quadratic. `many-blocks` and `unmatched-openers` (every list item opens a block that is auto-closed by the next item) target that; `long-block-body` is linear on both sides and serves as the baseline. The current package slices only the block lines with `state.getLines` and stays linear in the number of blocks; no superlinear path was found in it.
